```{python}
cell_id = ""
xenium_zarr = ""   # Path to your Zarr store
image_key = "morphology_focus"           # Key of the image element in the SpatialData object
table_key = "table"                      # Key of the AnnData table in the SpatialData object
cell_boundary_key = "cell_boundaries"    # Key for the cell boundary shapes element

cyto_channel = 1                         # Channel index for cytoplasm/cell body (e.g., ATP1A1)
cyto_channel_name = "ATP1A1/CD45/E-Cadherin"  # Channel name for spatialdata-plot rendering
nucleus_channel = 0                      # Channel index for nucleus (e.g., DAPI)
nucleus_channel_name = "DAPI"            # Channel name for spatialdata-plot rendering
segment_key = "segmented_cellpose"       # Key used to store segmentation output
crop_size = 600                          # Side length of the square crop in pixels
pixel_size = 0.2125                      # µm/px at pyramid level 0 (from pyramid metadata table)

# Cellpose parameters
diameter = None            # Expected cell diameter in pixels; None = auto-estimate
flow_threshold = 0.4       # Flow error threshold for filtering detections
cellprob_threshold = 0.0   # Minimum cell probability threshold
use_gpu = False            # Set to True if a CUDA-compatible GPU is available
```

```{python}
import numpy as np

import spatialdata as sd
import spatialdata_io
import spatialdata_plot  # registers the .pl accessor on SpatialData
from spatialdata.models import Labels2DModel
from spatialdata.transformations import Identity, Translation

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import squidpy as sq
from cellpose import models

print(f"SpatialData version:     {sd.__version__}")
print(f"spatialdata-io version:  {spatialdata_io.__version__}")
print(f"spatialdata-plot version:{spatialdata_plot.__version__}")
print(f"Squidpy version:         {sq.__version__}")
```

```{python}
sdata = sd.read_zarr(xenium_zarr)

_adata = sdata.tables[table_key]
print(f"Table '{table_key}': {_adata.n_obs} cells")

_img_ds = sdata.images[image_key]["scale0"].ds
_img_da = _img_ds[list(_img_ds.data_vars)[0]]
print(f"Image '{image_key}' shape (c, h, w): {tuple(_img_da.shape)}, dtype: {_img_da.dtype}")
```


```{python}
def cellpose_segmentation(
    arr: np.ndarray,
    cyto_channel_idx: int = 0,
    nucleus_channel_idx: int = 1,
    diameter: float = None,
    flow_threshold: float = 0.4,
    cellprob_threshold: float = 0.0,
    use_gpu: bool = False,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Run multi-channel Cellpose segmentation on an image array.

    Uses the Cellpose v4+ API (CellposeModel). Stacks the cytoplasm and nucleus
    channels into an (H, W, 2) array and passes channel_axis=2 so Cellpose
    treats them as cyto/nucleus inputs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    arr : np.ndarray
        Input image array (H, W, n_channels). Passed via channel=None in sq.im.segment;
        squidpy squeezes the C=1 dim before calling, leaving channels in the last axis.
    cyto_channel_idx : int
        Index of the cytoplasm/cell-body channel in arr.
    nucleus_channel_idx : int
        Index of the nucleus channel in arr.
    diameter : float or None
        Expected diameter of cells in pixels. If None, Cellpose auto-estimates.
    flow_threshold : float
        Flow error threshold for filtering cells.
    cellprob_threshold : float
        Minimum cell probability threshold.
    use_gpu : bool
        Whether to use GPU acceleration.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Integer label mask where each unique value > 0 is a segmented cell.
    """
    model = models.CellposeModel(gpu=use_gpu)

    # Stack to (H, W, 2): Cellpose v4 uses channel_axis instead of `channels`
    # squidpy squeezes the C=1 dim before calling, so arr arrives as (H, W, n_channels)
    cyto = arr[:, :, cyto_channel_idx]
    nucleus = arr[:, :, nucleus_channel_idx]
    img_2ch = np.stack([cyto, nucleus], axis=2)

    masks, flows, styles = model.eval(
        img_2ch,
        channel_axis=2,
        diameter=diameter,
        flow_threshold=flow_threshold,
        cellprob_threshold=cellprob_threshold,
    )

    return masks
```


```{python}
adata = sdata.tables[table_key]
coords = adata.obsm["spatial"]

image_ds = sdata.images[image_key]["scale0"].ds
image_da = image_ds[list(image_ds.data_vars)[0]]
img_h, img_w = image_da.shape[1], image_da.shape[2]

_pixel_size_x = pixel_size
_pixel_size_y = pixel_size
print(f"Pixel size: x={_pixel_size_x} µm/px, y={_pixel_size_y} µm/px")

# Convert spatial coords (µm) to pixel indices for out-of-bounds check.
pixel_coords = np.column_stack([coords[:, 0] / _pixel_size_x, coords[:, 1] / _pixel_size_y])

_x_oob = (pixel_coords[:,0] < 0).sum() + (pixel_coords[:,0] >= img_w).sum()
_y_oob = (pixel_coords[:,1] < 0).sum() + (pixel_coords[:,1] >= img_h).sum()
if _x_oob > 0 or _y_oob > 0:
    print(f"WARNING: {_x_oob} cells out of bounds in x, {_y_oob} out of bounds in y")
else:
    print("All pixel coordinates are within image bounds.")
```


```{python}
# Look up the centroid of the target cell from its boundary polygon
_cell_poly = sdata[cell_boundary_key].loc[cell_id].geometry
cx_phys, cy_phys = _cell_poly.centroid.x, _cell_poly.centroid.y
print(f"Cell '{cell_id}' centroid (physical): x={cx_phys:.2f} µm, y={cy_phys:.2f} µm")

# Convert centroid to pixel space and compute bounding box in pixel coords.
# The image has an Identity transform in spatialdata (global coord = pixel index),
# so bounding_box_query must receive pixel coordinates.
cx_px = cx_phys / _pixel_size_x
cy_px = cy_phys / _pixel_size_y
x_min = cx_px - crop_size / 2
x_max = cx_px + crop_size / 2
y_min = cy_px - crop_size / 2
y_max = cy_px + crop_size / 2
print(f"Cell '{cell_id}' centroid (pixel): x={cx_px:.1f}, y={cy_px:.1f}")
print(f"Crop bounding box (pixel): x=[{x_min:.1f}, {x_max:.1f}], y=[{y_min:.1f}, {y_max:.1f}]")

if x_min < 0 or y_min < 0 or x_max > img_w or y_max > img_h:
    print(f"WARNING: crop extends outside image bounds ({img_w} × {img_h} px)")
else:
    print("Crop is fully within image bounds.")

# Crop the full SpatialData object using spatialdata's bounding_box_query (physical coords).
# This crops images, labels, and shapes together so they remain aligned.
sdata_crop = sdata.query.bounding_box(
    axes=["x", "y"],
    min_coordinate=[x_min, y_min],
    max_coordinate=[x_max, y_max],
    target_coordinate_system="global",
)
print(f"Cropped SpatialData — images: {list(sdata_crop.images)}, labels: {list(sdata_crop.labels)}, shapes: {list(sdata_crop.shapes)}")

_all_crop_elements = {**sdata_crop.images, **sdata_crop.labels, **sdata_crop.shapes}
_missing = [k for k in ["cell_labels", cell_boundary_key] if k not in _all_crop_elements]
if _missing:
    print(f"WARNING: expected elements missing from crop: {_missing}")
```


```{python}
# Overview plot: whole tissue rendered by spatialdata-plot (auto-selects optimal pyramid level)
# with crop bounding box highlighted in physical (global) coordinates.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 8))
sdata.pl.render_images(image_key, channel=cyto_channel_name).pl.show(ax=ax, legend_loc=None, colorbar=False)
ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle(
    (x_min, y_min), crop_size, crop_size,
    linewidth=1.5, edgecolor="red", facecolor="none"
))
ax.set_title(f"Tissue overview ({cyto_channel_name}) — crop location for '{cell_id}'")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```


```{python}
# Crop plot: cyto and nucleus channels side by side with cell boundary polygon overlay.
# Build ImageContainer from the already-cropped image (needed for segmentation below).
_cropped_img_da = sd.get_pyramid_levels(sdata_crop[image_key], n=0)
print(f"_cropped_img_da type:  {type(_cropped_img_da)}")
print(f"_cropped_img_da dims:  {_cropped_img_da.dims}")
print(f"_cropped_img_da shape: {_cropped_img_da.shape}")
# Rename 'c' → 'channels' and add 'z' dim so squidpy gets the expected (channels, y, x, z) layout
_cropped_img_da = _cropped_img_da.rename({'c': 'channels'}).expand_dims('z', axis=-1)
img = sq.im.ImageContainer(_cropped_img_da, layer="image")

_poly_xs = np.array(_cell_poly.exterior.coords)[:, 0] / _pixel_size_x
_poly_ys = np.array(_cell_poly.exterior.coords)[:, 1] / _pixel_size_y

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 6))

for _ax, _ch_name, _title in [
    (axes[0], cyto_channel_name,    f"Cyto — {cyto_channel_name}"),
    (axes[1], nucleus_channel_name, f"Nucleus — {nucleus_channel_name}"),
]:
    sdata_crop.pl.render_images(image_key, channel=_ch_name).pl.show(ax=_ax, legend_loc=None, colorbar=False)
    _ax.plot(_poly_xs, _poly_ys, color="red", linewidth=1.5)
    _ax.set_title(f"{_title}\ncell '{cell_id}'")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```


```{python}
# Diagnostic: print per-channel shape and intensity stats before segmentation.
_cropped_arr = img["image"].data  # (H, W, Z, channels) — squidpy internal layout

print(f"ImageContainer layer 'image' shape (H, W, Z, channels): {tuple(_cropped_arr.shape)}")
for _idx, _name in [(cyto_channel, cyto_channel_name), (nucleus_channel, nucleus_channel_name)]:
    _ch = _cropped_arr[:, :, 0, _idx].compute()
    print(
        f"  channel {_idx} ({_name}): shape={_ch.shape}, "
        f"min={_ch.min():.1f}, max={_ch.max():.1f}, "
        f"p99={np.percentile(_ch, 99):.1f}"
    )
```


```{python}
# channel=None passes the full (H, W, C) array to cellpose_segmentation.
# cyto_channel_idx and nucleus_channel_idx are forwarded as fn_kwargs.
sq.im.segment(
    img,
    layer="image",
    channel=None,
    method=cellpose_segmentation,
    layer_added=segment_key,
    cyto_channel_idx=cyto_channel,
    nucleus_channel_idx=nucleus_channel,
    diameter=diameter,
    flow_threshold=flow_threshold,
    cellprob_threshold=cellprob_threshold,
    use_gpu=use_gpu,
)
```


```{python}
print(img)
print(f"Number of segments in crop: {len(np.unique(img[segment_key]))}")

_xenium_labels_ds = sdata_crop["cell_labels"]["scale0"].ds
_xenium_labels_da = _xenium_labels_ds[list(_xenium_labels_ds.data_vars)[0]]
_xenium_label_crop = _xenium_labels_da.values

_cellpose_label_crop = img[segment_key].data[:, :, 0, 0]

print(f"Xenium label shape:   {_xenium_label_crop.shape}")
print(f"Cellpose label shape: {tuple(_cellpose_label_crop.shape)}")
if _xenium_label_crop.shape != tuple(_cellpose_label_crop.shape):
    print("WARNING: shape mismatch — boundary overlays may not align.")

# Add Cellpose labels to sdata_crop so spatialdata-plot can render them
# alongside the Xenium labels in the same physical coordinate space.
sdata_crop.labels["cellpose_labels"] = Labels2DModel.parse(
    np.array(_cellpose_label_crop),
    dims=("y", "x"),
    transformations={"global": Translation([x_min, y_min], axes=("x", "y"))},
)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 4))

for _ax, _label_key, _title in [
    (axes[0], "cell_labels",      "Xenium segmentation"),
    (axes[1], "cellpose_labels",  "Cellpose segmentation"),
]:
    sdata_crop.pl.render_images(image_key, channel=cyto_channel_name)\
        .pl.render_labels(_label_key, fill_alpha=0, color="white")\
        .pl.show(ax=_ax, legend_loc=None, colorbar=False)
    _ax.set_title(_title)
```
